newsitem.title: UK: Panamax grain trade dominates dry cargo market.
newsitem.headline: Panamax grain trade dominates dry cargo market.

text.p: Grain trading has dominated Thursday's freight market with firmer rates reported on several key Panamax routes such as USGulf to Holland, USGulf to Japan and NoPac to Taiwan, brokers said.
The Baltic Freight Index accordingly jumped 10 points to 1450.

There was also a limited improvement in rates for owners of Handy-sizes in the Plate and Brazil but brokers reported an oversupply of early tonnage in the north Atlantic where prospects for owners of the older, smaller variety of Handy-sizes were said not to be very encouraging.
But large modern craned vessels were enjoying steadier demand in most areas and the Baltic Handy Index rose eight points to 1,016.
Andre's booking of Cho Yang tonnage for 54,000 tonnes heavy grain for March 10/20 at $26.00 basis no combination was reckoned by brokers to indicate a stronger market.
Another firmer booking was Cargill's fixture of Armia Krajowa for 60,000 heavy grain USGulf to Holland for end Feb at a lumpsum equivalent of $12.90.

In the minerals sector few caper fixtures emerged but market talk circulated that Baoshan Steel fixed SBC Express 211,000 dwt for iron ore from West Australia to China (possible at around $4.50), and Safore took Timawra 129,000 dwt for two laden legs, Norfolk to Richards Bay and Saldanha Bay to Continent iro ore, on private terms.

In Handy-sizes the gearless Premnitz 38,250 dwt was rumoured fixed by J.Lauritzen from the Continent via the Baltic to USGulf at $5,000/$5,500 daily but activity was limited in this area with brokers reporting plenty of small prompt handy tonnage availabnle.
